Class OnixEventScheduler

Namespace
OnixRuntime.Api.Events
Assembly
OnixRuntime.dll

Manages execution context switching for asynchronous operations to ensure code runs on the correct game thread or tick.

Remarks

This scheduler allows developers to sequence async logic that hops between background threads and specific game loops (e.g., Main Tick, Server Tick, or Render loops).

Key features include:

  • Context Switching: Awaitable methods to pause execution until the next specific game event occurs.
  • Fire-and-Forget Handling: Use HandleTask(Task) to execute tasks without blocking, ensuring exceptions are logged rather than crashing the application.
  • Game Utilities: Integrated helpers for managing inventory state and awaiting vanilla command responses.

Methods

ExecuteVanillaCommandWithResponse(string, CancellationToken)

Executes a game command asynchronously and waits for the result to come in. This only works for commands that return a proper response. Some servers use text packets instead for command output, making this function not work. But on a server that implemented commands responsibly, this is a great way to run a command and get the result of specifically that command in a split way. Uses a timeout of 20 seconds by default, which should be more than enough for any command to respond. If the timeout is reached without receiving a response, this function will return null.

public Task<VanillaCommandResponse?> ExecuteVanillaCommandWithResponse(string command, CancellationToken ct = default)

Parameters

command string

The command to run.

ct CancellationToken

A cancellation token to cancel the operation.

Returns

Task<VanillaCommandResponse>

A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains the command response, or null if the timeout is reached.

Examples

var testforCommandRes = await Scheduler.ExecuteVanillaCommandWithResponse("/testfor @e[rm=1]");
if (testforCommandRes is not null) {
    Console.WriteLine($"There are {testforCommandRes.SuccessCount} entities around you.");
    Console.WriteLine("They are: " + string.Join(", ", testforCommandRes.Messages
        .Where(x => x.MessageParams.Length > 0)
        .Select(x => x.MessageParams.LastOrDefault(""))));
    testforCommandRes.ShouldSilence = true;
}

Exceptions

OperationCanceledException

Whenever the cancellation token is canceled, but not when the timeout expires.

GetNextChatMessage(Func<ChatMessageAddedEventData, bool>, CancellationToken)

Waits for a chat message matching the predicate to be received and returns it. You can ensure it's the message you want to read and not a stray message as the chat can be quite unpredictable. This function will return null when the timeout is reached without receiving a message matching the predicate. The timeout is set to 10 seconds by default, which should be more than enough for any message to come in.

public Task<ChatMessageAddedEventData?> GetNextChatMessage(Func<ChatMessageAddedEventData, bool> isTheDesiredMessage, CancellationToken ct = default)

Parameters

isTheDesiredMessage Func<ChatMessageAddedEventData, bool>

A function returning true when the message is of interest to you.

ct CancellationToken

A cancellation token to cancel the wait early.

Returns

Task<ChatMessageAddedEventData>

A task of the message that matched or nullptr.

Examples

var msg = await Onix.Events.Scheduler.GetNextChatMessage(
    x => x.Content.Contains("among", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase),
    PluginEjectionCancellationToken);
if (msg is not null)
    Console.WriteLine("Got your message, it says " + msg.Content);
else
    Console.WriteLine("Timeout expired, i never got your message.");

Exceptions

OperationCanceledException

When the cancellation token is triggered, the timeout will not throw this exception.

HandleTask(Action)

Takes ownership of a task that you don't have anywhere to await but still want to ensure that any exceptions it throws are caught and logged, preventing unhandled exceptions from crashing the game. This variant lets you use an async lambda directly without needing Run(Action).

Parameters

The task you want to run in the background without tending to it.

OpenInventory(CancellationToken)

Await this task to open the inventory and get a ContainerScreen in the Container Tick context. This is a convenience function combining opening the player's inventory and letting you make changes.

public Task<ContainerScreen> OpenInventory(CancellationToken ct = default)

Parameters

ct CancellationToken

A cancellation token to prevent the operation from completing or stalling if the plugin is ejected or reloaded.

Returns

Task<ContainerScreen>

A task that completes once the inventory has been opened or the operation was cancelled.

Examples

ContainerScreen container = await Onix.Events.Scheduler.OpenInventory(PluginEjectionCancellationToken);
if (container.GetItem("hotbar_items", 0) is { IsEmpty: false } stack1 && container.GetItem("hotbar_items", 1) is { IsEmpty: false } stack2) {
    // This animation won't even be visible to almost everyone.
    container.SendFlyingItem(stack1, "hotbar_items", 0, "hotbar_items", 1);
    container.SendFlyingItem(stack2, "hotbar_items", 1, "hotbar_items", 0);
    // Switch the first and second hotbar slots
    container.TakeAll("hotbar_items", 0);
    container.PlaceAll("hotbar_items", 1);
    container.PlaceAll("hotbar_items", 0);
    // (Optional) Leave the inventory because we did our changes.
}
Onix.Gui.CloseCurrentScreen();
// Return to a threadpool thread for the rest if there is more to your function.
await Onix.Events.Scheduler.ExitCallback();

Remarks

Most functions in ContainerScreen still require trust, if you're trying to read items, you can read the player's inventory instead.

OpenInventoryCallback(Action<ContainerScreen>, CancellationToken)

Opens the inventory and runs a callback with ContainerScreen when it is opened. This is a convenience function combining opening the player's inventory and letting you make changes.

public void OpenInventoryCallback(Action<ContainerScreen> callback, CancellationToken ct = default)

Parameters

callback Action<ContainerScreen>

The callback to run once the inventory opens.

ct CancellationToken

A cancellation token to prevent the operation from completing or stalling if the plugin is ejected or reloaded.

Examples

Onix.Events.Scheduler.OpenInventoryCallback((container) => {
    // This animation won't even be visible to almost everyone.
    if (container.GetItem("hotbar_items", 0) is { IsEmpty: false } stack1 && container.GetItem("hotbar_items", 1) is { IsEmpty: false } stack2) {
        container.SendFlyingItem(stack1, "hotbar_items", 0, "hotbar_items", 1);
        container.SendFlyingItem(stack2, "hotbar_items", 1, "hotbar_items", 0);
        // Switch the first and second hotbar slots
        container.TakeAll("hotbar_items", 0);
        container.PlaceAll("hotbar_items", 1);
        container.PlaceAll("hotbar_items", 0);
    }
    // (Optional) Leave the inventory because we did our changes.
    Onix.Gui.CloseCurrentScreen();
}, PluginEjectionCancellationToken);

ScheduleInServerTick(int, Action, CancellationToken)

Allows you to run a callback on the next server tick without having to manually await the switch. This is useful for fire-and-forget style operations that still need to run on the main thread.

public void ScheduleInServerTick(int ticksToWait, Action callback, CancellationToken ct = default)

Parameters

ticksToWait int

The number of server ticks to wait before executing the callback. Must be a positive integer, 0 will execute on the next tick.

callback Action

The callback to execute on the next server tick.

ct CancellationToken

A cancellation token to cancel the operation.

Examples

Onix.Events.Scheduler.ScheduleNextServerTick(() => {
    // You know, sometimes you wake up and choose violence, cause a little genocide here and there, it happens, it really does.
    foreach (Entity entity in Onix.LocalServer!.World.Entities) {
        entity.Kill();
    }
    // Wait 5 ticks to let the items and experience orbs drop, then kill those.
    await Onix.Events.Scheduler.SwitchToServerTick(5, PluginEjectionCancellationToken); 
    foreach (Entity entity in Onix.LocalServer!.World.Entities) {
        entity.Kill();
    }

ScheduleInTick(int, Action, CancellationToken)

Allows you to run a callback on the next ticksToWait client tick without having to manually await the switch. This is useful for fire-and-forget style operations that still need to run on the main thread.

public void ScheduleInTick(int ticksToWait, Action callback, CancellationToken ct = default)

Parameters

ticksToWait int

The number of ticks to wait before executing the callback. Must be a positive integer, 0 will execute on the next tick.

callback Action

The callback to execute on the next client tick.

ct CancellationToken

A cancellation token to cancel the operation.

Examples

Onix.Events.Scheduler.ScheduleNextTick(() => {
    // If we're facing a block, break it if it's an oak log.
    // This only happens once, but at that time, we can't stand to look at oak logs I guess.
    // There are plenty of things you could do by now being in the tick but that's for you to decide, I'm breaking an oak logs potentially.
    if (Onix.LocalPlayer is { GameMode: GameMode.Creative, Raycast: { Type: RaycastResultType.Block } }) {
        Block facingBlock = Onix.LocalPlayer.Region.GetBlock(Onix.LocalPlayer.Raycast.BlockPosition);
        if (facingBlock is { NameFull: "minecraft:oak_log" }) {
            Onix.LocalPlayer.BreakBlock(Onix.LocalPlayer.Raycast);
            // wait 40 ticks or 2 seconds, then apologize for breaking the log.
            await Onix.Events.Scheduler.SwitchToTick(40, PluginEjectionCancellationToken);
            Onix.Gui.SetTitleText("Okay... I'm sorry for breaking your log...");
        }
    }
}, PluginEjectionCancellationToken);

SwitchToNextDirect2DRender(CancellationToken)

Await this task to switch to the next direct 2d render. (RendererDirect2D gfx, float delta) = await Onix.Events.Scheduler.SwitchToNextDirect2DRender(PluginEjectionCancellationToken);

SwitchToNextServerTick(CancellationToken)

Await this task to switch to the next server tick. Any code you write after this will now run in the context of the main server tick, allowing you to call game functions at the right time. Make sure to return to the thread pool with ExitCallback() if you need to do any heavy work to avoid freezing the game. You can also use HandleTask(Task) to run tasks in the background without awaiting them.

public Task SwitchToNextServerTick(CancellationToken ct = default)

Parameters

ct CancellationToken

A cancellation token to cancel the operation.

Returns

Task

A task that completes on the next server tick.

Examples

await Onix.Events.Scheduler.SwitchToNextServerTick(PluginEjectionCancellationToken);
// You know, sometimes you wake up and choose violence, cause a little genocide here and there, it happens, it really does.
foreach (Entity entity in Onix.LocalServer!.World.Entities) {
    entity.Kill();
}
// Exit the tick since our work here is done.
await Onix.Events.Scheduler.ExitCallback();

Exceptions

OperationCanceledException

WaitForServerPlayerPluginMessage(OnixPluginBase, CancellationToken)

Waits for a plugin message sent by a player to the local server until 5 seconds have passed.

public Task<ServerPlayerPluginMessageEventData?> WaitForServerPlayerPluginMessage(OnixPluginBase plugin, CancellationToken ct = default)

Parameters

plugin OnixPluginBase

Your plugin instance, for the cancellation token and identity.

ct CancellationToken

A cancellation token to cancel the operation, by default taken from plugin.

Returns

Task<ServerPlayerPluginMessageEventData>

A task that represents the asynchronous operation. The task result contains the message event data including the sending player, or null if the timeout is reached.

Examples

ServerPlayerPluginMessageEventData? msg = await Onix.Events.Scheduler.WaitForServerPlayerPluginMessage(this);
if (msg is not null) {
    string content = msg.IsString ? msg.ContentString! : $"{msg.ContentBytes!.Length} bytes";
    Console.WriteLine($"{msg.Sender.Name} sent: {content}");
} else {
    Console.WriteLine("Timeout expired, no player plugin message received.");
}

Exceptions

OperationCanceledException

Whenever the cancellation token is canceled, but not when the timeout expires.
